prompt: cal.py computes month lengths but is_leap(y) is wrong for century years. Fix is_leap to follow the Gregorian rule (a year is a leap year if divisible by 4, except centuries, which must be divisible by 400) so that days_in_month(y, m) is correct for any year and month 1..12. Keep both function names and signatures.
check:
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import calendar
from cal import days_in_month, is_leap
for y in [1600, 1700, 1900, 1999, 2000, 2001, 2004, 2024, 2100, 2400]:
    for m in range(1, 13):
        got, want = days_in_month(y, m), calendar.monthrange(y, m)[1]
        assert got == want, (y, m, got, want)
assert is_leap(2000) and is_leap(2024) and is_leap(1600)
assert not is_leap(1900) and not is_leap(2100) and not is_leap(2001)
print("ok")
